'''Vietnamese fish sauce''' is a dipping sauce prepared for use at the table. It contains a more concentrated fish sauce of a similar name.  

==Ingredients==
*¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Fish Sauce|nước mắm (concentrated fish sauce)]]
*1½ cups water
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|lemon juice]]
*1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]] or about 2 cloves pressed through a garlic press
*½ tsp [[Cookbook:Chili Paste|sambal oelek]] (a type of hot chile sauce)

==Procedure==
#Mix all ingredients together.
#If desired, bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] that cannot be stirred down.
#Cover and refrigerate.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*In restaurants it is served in small bowls, one for each diner, often with a bit of [[Cookbook:Julienne|julienned]] [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]] on top. It is sometimes served with rolls of various types (summer rolls, spring rolls, Imperial rolls, etc.) and is usually available in Vietnamese restaurants upon request.
*For home use, some prefer to store it in a squirt bottle and grind the sambal oelek and garlic to a smaller size using a mortar and pestle so that they do not clog the nozzle.
*You may find the smell quite strong in making this, especially if you decide to boil. Persevere.
*The Three Crabs Brand of concentrated fish sauce is universally praised. There are many, many other brands.
